name: wz-owl-stair-down
label: wizarding_world stairs wz-owl-stair-down (DOWN)
reasons: 화풍: 윤곽이 근흑(재질 어두운 톤 아님) (4/4)

surfaces.part: wooden frame / floor border around the opening
dark pit interior with far step silhouettes

answer.evidence: The whole sprite is a flat square floor plate, 29 px wide and rows 3-29. It has a wooden border (rows 3-7 across the top, plus the side columns) around a dark recessed opening (rows 8-14). Stone steps inside the opening are stacked as horizontal bands, with lighter edge lines at rows 19 and 24 and darker bands below them at rows 20-22. These bands show the stair descent drawn as a plan view. The object has no standing south face: the frame has no vertical front wall, and the width stays at 28-29 px from row 3 to row 28 with no receding side face. It reads as a flat decal or plate, not a volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: Density is not the problem: the candidate has 11 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving and 3 for the grass, and 0% near-flat coverage. The weak point is the outline. 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the dark edge reads as a near-black line, not a dark tone of the neighbouring material. The paving reference is at 80% neutral and the grass at 0%, so the candidate sits above both. The piece is a small framed icon, one tile of wood frame around grey steps, boxed in by that dark border, which gives the sticker look. It is not a continuous ground surface like the references. It has about 5 shading steps spread over the frame and stairs, with little grain or per-stone variation inside the steps. Because the dark outline is neutral and the whole piece is boxed in, I fail it on the outline and sticker-like construction despite the good tone count.

surfaces.part: wooden frame and pit opening seen from above
descending stair treads inside the frame

answer.evidence: This is a square floor decal, 29 px wide and about 27 rows tall, with a uniform wooden frame on all sides. Inside is a dark pit with stacked stair treads (edge lines at rows 15, 19 and 24) that read as plan-view steps going down. The bottom frame rows (27-29) are a thin border, not a vertical front face. The width profile is constant at 28-29 from row 3 to row 29, with no taper and no receding side face. The object has no front face of 3 or more rows, so it reads as a flat plate viewed from above.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, roughly one-tile framed stairwell icon, not a 4x3 ground patch, so it does not match the grass/paving references in kind or coverage. It reads as a boxed sticker: a wood-toned frame around a dark opening with a few grey steps. The measured facts show 100% neutral dark edge pixels, which supports a near-black outline and not the tinted material-tone edges the references use (grass 0% neutral). The 11 visible tones per tile beat the grass (3) and are close to the paving (7). But the 13 total colours are spread over only about 3 shading steps per material, in the frame, the interior and the steps. There is no per-element grain or clumping, and the surface has none of the paving's stone-by-stone shading. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. Overall it is shallower than the Beodeul standard and uses a sticker-style dark outline.

surfaces.part: wooden frame border around the opening

Below the pit are three stepped bands (rows 15-18, 19-23, 24-28), separated by light edge lines at rows 19 and 24. The silhouette width is a constant 28-29 across rows 3-28, so there is no receding side face and no separate vertical south face of 3 or more rows. The light lines at rows 19 and 24 are stair-tread edges inside the plate, not a front face of a standing volume. This matches a flat floor hatch, consistent with the 'flat' kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single framed stair tile, not a 4x3 ground patch, so it is a poor match for the grass and paving references. It has only 13 colours in total, and the brown frame and grey steps have about 3 lightness steps each, against roughly 5-6 in the references. The measured 100% near-neutral dark edge pixels, together with the dark rim in the image, point to a near-black sticker-style outline. The references use tinted or dark-material edges: grass has 0% neutral and paving 80%. The 11 visible tones per tile beat the grass (3) and are above the paving (7), but they come from a few contrasting blocks (frame, dark opening, steps) with little grain, scallop or per-stone shading. The piece reads as a flat icon, not a textured Beodeul surface, and when in doubt it fails.

surfaces.part: wooden frame border around the opening
dark stairwell opening with a far wall and shelf-like steps
stone steps descending, each with a light edge line

answer.evidence: The whole 29-wide, 26-row sprite (rows 3-28) is a rectangular decal. A light and dark wooden frame (rows 3-7 and the side columns) encloses a dark opening (rows 8-14) with stepped stone treads below it (light lines at rows 15, 19 and 24, each followed by darker rows). The steps look like a plan or inset view of a stair going down. No south face of 3 or more rows stands above the ground, and there is no eave or ellipse top. The object lies flat in the ground like a floor hatch or floor decal, which matches the flat kind. It reads as a top-down plate, not a standing 3/4 volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single-tile stairwell prop in a wooden frame, not a 4x3 ground patch like the grass and paving references, so the kind match is weak. Measured density is fine: 11 visible tones per tile against 3 for grass and 7 for paving, with 0% near-flat coverage. The weak point is the outline. 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, and by eye the dark border and stair interior read as a uniform black/grey line rather than a dark brown beside the wood. The grass reference is 0% neutral and the paving reference is 80%. Shading is shallow, with about 3 steps on the brown frame and 3-4 on the grey steps, against 5-6 on Beodeul materials. The result has the sticker-like look the standard rejects.
